ussdPage.heroDesc: We are preparing a USSD pilot so farmers can sell on ShambaNi even without a smartphone or internet connection. The goal is simple: dial a code on a basic phone and reach buyers as districts onboard.
ussdPage.step1Desc: After regulatory and network approval, participating farmers will receive the allocated pilot code and instructions. The current screen is a menu prototype only.
ussdPage.step2Desc: A simple menu appears on your screen. Choose what you want to do: list produce, check orders, or see your payments. Use number keys to navigate.
ussdPage.step3Desc: The proposed flow would send an SMS order notice. Payment arrangements will use an approved provider and will be confirmed separately during the pilot.
ussdPage.smsMockup: New order! Buyer wants 5 trays of eggs. Total: UGX 57,500. Reply CONFIRM to accept.
ussdPage.exploreDesc: This interactive screen demonstrates the intended menu. It is not connected to a mobile network.
ussdPage.langDesc: The menu prototype supports four languages. Telecom availability has not yet been activated.
ussdPage.sms1Content: New order received! John M. wants 10kg of tomatoes from your farm. Reply CONFIRM to accept or CANCEL to decline. — ShambaNi
ussdPage.sms2Content: Sample only: a future SMS could confirm an approved pilot payout after delivery.
ussdPage.sms3Content: This week's prices: Tomatoes UGX 3,500/kg (↑5%), Eggs UGX 11,500/tray (→), Matooke UGX 15,000/bunch (↓3%). List your produce now!
ussdPage.faqQ1: Does USSD cost money to use?
ussdPage.faqA1: Pricing will be confirmed with the selected telecom or licensed aggregator before the pilot opens.
ussdPage.faqA2: The proposed service is designed for basic and smart phones that support USSD. Actual availability will depend on the approved network connection.
ussdPage.faqQ3: How do I receive payments without a bank account?
ussdPage.faqA3: The pilot payment process has not been activated. ShambaNi will use an approved payment provider and will never ask for a mobile-money PIN.
ussdPage.faqQ4: Can I change my listed prices via USSD?
ussdPage.faqA4: This is a proposed feature. Price updates will be tested after the approved USSD service and secure backend are connected.
ussdPage.faqQ5: How will I know when someone orders my produce?
ussdPage.faqA5: The proposed flow includes SMS alerts. Messages will begin only after the telecom integration has been approved and tested.
ussdPage.faqA6: No production farmer or payment data is collected through this USSD prototype. Security and privacy controls must pass review before the pilot opens.
ussdPage.ctaDesc: Review the proposed menu or email your interest. No ShambaNi short code is active yet.

aboutPage.heroTitle: Testing a more inclusive farmer marketplace in Uganda
aboutPage.heroDesc: ShambaNi exists to bridge the gap between rural farmers and urban markets. We believe that every farmer — whether they own a smartphone or a basic feature phone — deserves access to a thriving marketplace.
aboutPage.storyPara1: It started with a simple observation: millions of farmers across East Africa grow incredible produce, yet many struggle to find buyers. Meanwhile, urban consumers, schools, and restaurants search endlessly for fresh, affordable, locally-grown food. The disconnect isn't about quality — it's about connection.
aboutPage.storyPara2: ShambaNi is developing a feature-phone path because a website alone will not reach every farmer. The current USSD screens demonstrate the intended menu while regulatory, telecom and backend work continues.
aboutPage.storyPara3: The current product is a Uganda-focused pre-pilot prototype. Mpigi and Wakiso are the proposed first districts. Regional expansion and additional languages remain future goals.
aboutPage.pullQuote: Technology should adapt to the farmer. Not the other way around.
aboutPage.why1Desc: The proposed USSD service is designed for basic phones. It is not active and no short code has been allocated to ShambaNi.
aboutPage.why2Desc: One of the lowest fees in the region. We believe farmers should keep what they earn. The rest goes straight to growing their farm.
aboutPage.why3Desc: The pilot starts in Uganda. Expansion to Kenya, Tanzania and Rwanda will be considered only after the Uganda operating model is proven.
aboutPage.paymentsDesc: Payment options shown on this prototype describe the proposed pilot flow. No payment processor or escrow service is currently integrated.
aboutPage.paymentAirtel: Proposed option subject to provider agreement
aboutPage.paymentMtn: Proposed option subject to provider agreement
aboutPage.paymentBank: Manual pilot option subject to approval
aboutPage.hiw1Desc: During the controlled pilot, approved farmers will be onboarded through a secure web or assisted process. USSD will follow regulatory and telecom approval.
aboutPage.hiw2Desc: Schools, businesses, and households browse fresh produce and place orders directly with farmers.
aboutPage.hiw3Desc: Delivery and payment terms will be confirmed manually during the pilot. No integrated payment or escrow service is currently live.
aboutPage.visionText: By 2028, ShambaNi aims to connect 10,000 farmers across East Africa, process UGX 5 billion in transactions, and expand to all major agricultural districts in the region. We envision a future where no farmer is left behind because of the phone they own — where USSD, web, and mobile work together to create the most inclusive agricultural marketplace in Africa.
aboutPage.founderQuote: I built ShambaNi because I saw my own family struggle to sell their produce. My uncle would travel for hours to find a buyer for his bananas, often returning with nothing. Technology should solve this, not make it harder. That's why USSD is at the heart of everything we do.
aboutPage.ctaDesc: Whether you're a farmer ready to sell or a buyer looking for the freshest produce — we're here to connect you.
